notes: S332 nine-axis website audit led to a founder-authorized, blast-radius-scoped public deployment without weakening the identity gate. Every emitted item names a conversion or information-finding outcome, reuses existing RUM/link/CTA infrastructure, adds no dependency, and preserves privacy floors. Three novel reserve candidates were generated but not emitted because the carried, premise-verified items compound the current release truth more directly.

items.title: Sample canonical product destinations without letting network uncertainty lie
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: audit-site-links validates host shape and internal existence but never tests whether registry-owned external product destinations answer; S331 fixed several real stale destinations manually. Outcome: visitors reach the intended product in one click, while release reviewers can distinguish a confirmed dead target from an unavailable probe instead of interpreting silence as health.
items.recipe: Extend the import-safe link court with a bounded canonical-destination sampler sourced only from registry-owned external product links; classify each observation as passed, failed, or unknown; require repeated deterministic failure before a dead verdict; make network unavailability explicit and non-passing; write a public-safe aggregate receipt with no visitor data; add self-tests for redirects, timeouts, transient 5xx, and confirmed dead destinations; keep the deterministic build court offline by validating receipt shape and freshness rather than performing live HTTP.

L1.recipe: Add pure three-state classification helpers and a small explicit destination set.

L2.recipe: L1 plus bounded live sampling, public receipt, freshness check, self-tests, and release integration.

L3.recipe: L2 plus append-only reachability history and change-risk prioritization.

executionLog.result: Shipped a bounded sampler over the public registry projection, an offline freshness/shape court, a four-hour refresh lane, public status projection, and a status-proof/evidence-graph edge. The first live receipt reports 10/12 passed, 0 failed, and 2 unknown; 401 and repeated 503 observations remain unknown rather than green or dead.
executionLog.verification: self-test 9/9; receipt check current; publish cascades 30/30 closed; build-gate reachability 245/245

items.title: Publish privacy-thresholded interruption pressure by surface and visit depth
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: VSAttention emits an in-browser vs:attention-claimed event, but no RUM listener consumes it and rollup-rum-ux has no attention family. Outcome: the studio can tell whether the one-surface budget reduces interruptions for new and returning visitors without storing a browser history, while a sparse cohort remains honestly dark.
items.recipe: Emit one allowlisted attention:claimed event through the existing /v/rum path with a bounded label composed from a fixed surface enum and coarse visit-depth bucket; reject arbitrary labels at the Worker; aggregate only day/surface/depth counts from committed RUM history; suppress every cohort below the existing privacy floor; publish a public-safe attention-pressure receipt and status projection; add positive/negative self-tests proving no route, identifier, session key, or free text reaches the artifact.

L1.recipe: Wire the bounded claim event into the existing RUM transport and allowlist.

L2.recipe: L1 plus privacy-thresholded rollup, public receipt, status projection, and regression tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus pre/post release pressure comparison and an abstaining trend history.

executionLog.result: Shipped fixed-vocabulary post-consent claim telemetry, edge rejection of arbitrary labels, privacy-floor aggregation, a public-safe receipt, status projection, and build/status-proof integration. Cookie consent remains deliberately excluded.
executionLog.verification: worker unit 53/53; attention contract 15/15; RUM allowlist self-test 10/10 and 190 emit call-sites synchronized; rollup self-test 36 assertions; receipt self-test 6/6

items.title: Make CTA readiness name the age of the evidence behind it
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: check-cta-readiness reports observedThrough and correctly abstains when no post-epoch span exists, but a frozen source reads like a merely young window rather than stale evidence. Outcome: operators immediately know whether a conversion decision lacks time or lacks fresh observations, reducing false waits and making the next release action findable.
items.recipe: Derive an evidenceAgeDays value from the committed source asOf date, keep wall-clock age out of byte-reproducibility comparisons, render a distinct stale-evidence explanation when the source date falls beyond the declared window, and add self-tests for current, young, stale, and absent evidence.

L1.recipe: Add the source-derived age and four-state self-test coverage.

L2.recipe: L1 plus public CTA surface copy and status projection.

L3.recipe: L2 plus age trend history and alert routing.

executionLog.result: Shipped current/aging/stale/absent evidence-age states in the readiness court and a browser-derived public status tile. Wall-clock age remains outside byte-reproducibility comparisons while the committed observedThrough source stays covered.
executionLog.verification: CTA readiness self-test 15 checks; deterministic --check current
